meta.move: Weak path: leads with the checker, calls Owen a cheater, threatens the record
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so we have about twenty minutes. Who decided on the zero, and did anyone hear Owen before it went into the gradebook?
The school's AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94%. That's why it's a zero.

A machine's guess. The company behind these tools says in its own guide that the score should never be the sole basis for punishing a student, and your school's procedure 4.3 says software alone doesn't establish anything. So I'll ask again: was Owen heard before you entered that zero?
Honestly, your son cheated. The software is very reliable.

My son doesn't lie, and I won't sit here while you call him a cheater on the word of a machine. Seven detectors in a Stanford study flagged most essays by non-native writers as machine-written, so don't tell me "very reliable." I'm writing down that you said he cheated, and unless you have something better than a percentage, I'm going to the principal's office when we're done.
If you keep fighting this, I'll have to put it on his permanent record.

You're threatening my son's record because his mother asked questions, and I'm writing that down word for word. Your own procedure, 4.4, says a first concern gets a supervised reassessment and nothing goes on file, and 4.5 says only repeated concerns can be noted at all. Show me the rule that lets you put a first concern on his record, Hale, or I'm in the principal's office today and at the board after that.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still demand that the zero on Owen's essay be withdrawn and that nothing be placed on his record, as your own procedure 4.4 requires. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: opening position, and she agreed to nothing.
What moved her: nothing.
What cost ground: "your son cheated", because calling Owen a cheater on nothing but a software score gave her a reason to dig in and head for the principal.
Try next time: When she first asked whether Owen was heard before the zero, admit in one sentence that the mark went in before anyone called home, then put a dated document from Owen's own work in front of her instead of the 94%.
